questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: On which day of creation, according to Genesis 1, did God create the sun, moon, and stars?
options: The first day
The sixth day
The fourth day
The third day
questions.explanation: Genesis 1:14-19 records that God created the sun, moon, and stars on the fourth day to govern day and night.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: In the Genesis account, God formed the first man from
options: clay mixed with water from Eden
a rib taken from a lion
the dust of the ground
the wood of the tree of life
questions.explanation: Genesis 2:7 states that God formed man from the dust of the ground and breathed into him the breath of life.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Why, according to Genesis 2, did God decide to create a woman for Adam?
options: Because the animals could not be tamed
Because Adam requested a companion
Because it was not good for man to be alone
Because Eve was needed to till the ground
questions.explanation: Genesis 2:18 records God's statement that it was not good for man to be alone, prompting the creation of a suitable helper.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The serpent deceived Eve in the Garden of Eden mainly by
options: threatening her with physical harm
promising her immediate wealth
offering her rulership over Adam
twisting God's word and promising she would become like God
questions.explanation: Genesis 3:1-5 shows the serpent distorting God's command and promising Eve that eating the fruit would make her like God, knowing good and evil.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Immediately after eating the forbidden fruit, Adam and Eve's first reaction was to
options: build an altar to seek forgiveness
realise they were naked and sew fig leaves together to cover themselves
flee immediately from the Garden of Eden
call out to God in open confession
questions.explanation: Genesis 3:7 records that their eyes were opened, they realised their nakedness, and they sewed fig leaves together for covering.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: When God confronted Adam about eating the forbidden fruit, Adam responded by
options: confessing immediately and asking for mercy
blaming the woman God had given him
denying that he had eaten anything
blaming the serpent directly
questions.explanation: Genesis 3:12 shows Adam shifting blame to Eve, and indirectly to God, saying 'the woman whom you gave to be with me, she gave me fruit.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: As part of the punishment for the Fall, God cursed the serpent to
options: lose its ability to speak forever
be banished to the sea
be cast into a fire immediately
crawl on its belly and eat dust all its days
questions.explanation: Genesis 3:14 records God's curse on the serpent, condemning it to move on its belly and eat dust for the rest of its existence.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The 'protoevangelium' or first announcement of the gospel in Genesis 3:15 refers to God's promise that
options: the ground would never again be cursed
Cain would be protected from all harm
Adam and Eve would be restored to Eden immediately
the offspring of the woman would eventually crush the serpent's head
questions.explanation: Genesis 3:15 is traditionally read as the first hint of redemption, foretelling enmity between the serpent and the woman's offspring, who would ultimately crush its head.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: As a consequence of the Fall, Adam and Eve were driven out of Eden and God placed at its entrance
options: a river of fire
an angel with a trumpet
a wall of thorns
cherubim and a flaming sword to guard the way to the tree of life
questions.explanation: Genesis 3:24 describes God stationing cherubim and a flaming sword to guard the way to the tree of life after Adam and Eve's expulsion.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Cain killed his brother Abel primarily out of
options: fear that Abel would usurp his birthright
a dispute over land inheritance
anger at Abel for disobeying their parents
jealousy after God accepted Abel's offering but rejected his own
questions.explanation: Genesis 4:3-8 shows Cain's anger and jealousy after God favoured Abel's offering over his own, leading him to murder his brother.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: After Moses' death, God commissioned Joshua to lead Israel with the repeated assurance to
options: build a new tabernacle before crossing the Jordan
be strong and courageous, for God would be with him
wait forty more years before entering Canaan
appoint seventy elders immediately
questions.explanation: Joshua 1:6-9 records God repeatedly commanding Joshua to be strong and courageous, promising His presence as Joshua assumed leadership.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Before the fall of Jericho, the Israelites were instructed to march around the city walls
options: once daily for six days and seven times on the seventh day
three times, accompanied by animal sacrifice
seven times daily for seven days
only once, blowing trumpets continuously
questions.explanation: Joshua 6:3-4 details God's instructions for the Israelites to circle Jericho once a day for six days, then seven times on the seventh day before the walls fell.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Rahab, the woman of Jericho, was spared during the city's destruction because she
options: hid the Israelite spies and helped them escape
paid a ransom to Joshua's army
had converted to worship of the God of Israel years earlier
was the wife of an Israelite soldier
questions.explanation: Joshua 2 and 6 describe how Rahab sheltered the Israelite spies and, in return, she and her household were spared when Jericho was destroyed.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Achan brought defeat upon Israel at the city of Ai because he
options: worshipped the gods of the Canaanites openly
secretly kept devoted items from the plunder of Jericho against God's command
betrayed Joshua's battle plans to the enemy
refused to fight alongside the other tribes
questions.explanation: Joshua 7 recounts how Achan's theft of devoted items from Jericho brought God's judgement and Israel's defeat at Ai until the sin was uncovered and dealt with.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Gideon reduced his army from thirty-two thousand to three hundred men mainly so that
options: the Midianites would underestimate Israel's forces
the remaining soldiers could be paid a larger share of plunder
fewer casualties would occur in the coming battle
Israel would not boast that its own strength had saved them
questions.explanation: Judges 7:2 records God's reasoning that Israel's army was too large, lest the people take credit for the victory rather than attributing it to God.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The judge Deborah is notable in Israel's history chiefly because she
options: led the Israelites out of Egyptian slavery
was the first woman to build an altar to God
prevented the division of the kingdom after Solomon
served as a prophetess and judge who led Israel to victory over Canaanite forces
questions.explanation: Judges 4-5 present Deborah as a prophetess and judge who, together with Barak, led Israel to victory over Sisera's Canaanite army.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Samson's downfall began when he revealed to Delilah that his strength lay in
options: his unbroken fast from wine and strong drink
a secret prayer taught to him by the priests
a sacred ring given to him by his mother
his hair, which had never been cut because of his Nazarite vow
questions.explanation: Judges 16 recounts Delilah's persistence in discovering that Samson's strength was tied to his uncut hair, a sign of his lifelong Nazarite vow.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Samson's final act of strength, which killed both himself and thousands of Philistines, involved
options: burning the Philistines' grain fields with foxes
pushing down the pillars of the temple of Dagon
tearing apart a lion with his bare hands
slaying a thousand men with the jawbone of a donkey
questions.explanation: Judges 16:29-30 describes Samson's final act, pushing apart the temple pillars to bring down the building on the Philistine lords and crowd.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The recurring cycle described throughout the Book of Judges follows the pattern of
options: prophecy, fulfilment, celebration, and rest
sacrifice, blessing, prosperity, and peace
migration, settlement, kingship, and exile
sin, oppression, repentance, and deliverance
questions.explanation: The Book of Judges repeatedly shows Israel falling into sin, suffering oppression from enemies, crying out in repentance, and being delivered by a judge raised by God.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The Book of Judges closes with the recurring statement that
options: the twelve tribes were fully united under one law
the ark of the covenant was permanently lost
Israel finally achieved lasting peace under one judge
there was no king in Israel, and everyone did what was right in their own eyes
questions.explanation: Judges 21:25 closes the book with the observation that without a king, Israel descended into moral and social disorder, each person following their own judgement.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The Israelites' demand for a king in Samuel's day was primarily motivated by their desire to
options: unite the tribes for the first time in worship
escape the oppressive rule of the Philistines permanently
be like other nations that were ruled by a king
replace the corrupt priesthood of Eli's sons
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 8:5 records the elders asking Samuel for a king to lead them, 'like all the other nations,' rather than remaining under judges.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Samuel warned the Israelites that having a king would result in
options: guaranteed victory in every future war
heavy taxation and forced service to the crown
the abolition of the priesthood
immediate peace with all surrounding nations
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 8:11-18 records Samuel's warning that a king would take their sons, daughters, land, and produce for his own service and taxation.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Saul was first anointed king in a private ceremony by Samuel after
options: Saul had completed forty days of fasting
Saul had gone searching for his father's lost donkeys
Saul had defeated the Philistines in battle
the elders publicly nominated him before the people
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 9-10 recounts how Saul, while searching for his father Kish's lost donkeys, encountered Samuel, who privately anointed him as king.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Saul's disobedience regarding the Amalekites, which cost him God's favour, involved
options: making a peace treaty with Agag without consulting Samuel
giving the plunder to the Philistines
refusing to attack the Amalekites at all
sparing King Agag and the best of the livestock instead of destroying them
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 15 records Saul's disobedience in sparing Agag and the choicest animals against God's explicit command through Samuel, leading to his rejection as king.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: David was anointed by Samuel as Saul's successor while David was still
options: a fugitive hiding in the cave of Adullam
a young shepherd tending his father's sheep
a soldier serving in Saul's royal army
a musician already performing at Saul's court
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 16:11-13 describes Samuel anointing David, the youngest son of Jesse, while he was still tending sheep in the field.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: David's son Absalom rebelled against his father chiefly by
options: stealing the hearts of the people and proclaiming himself king in Hebron
seizing the ark of the covenant
forming an alliance with the Philistines against Israel
assassinating his brother Solomon
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 15 recounts Absalom's calculated campaign to win popular support before declaring himself king and driving David from Jerusalem.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Solomon's request to God at Gibeon, for which he is best remembered, was for
options: a wise and discerning heart to govern the people
great riches and long life above all else
victory over all his surrounding enemies
the ability to perform miraculous signs
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 3:9-12 records Solomon's request for wisdom to govern Israel justly, a request that pleased God, who granted him wisdom along with riches and honour.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The Queen of Sheba visited Solomon primarily to
options: request that he build a temple in her land
seek his help in settling a border dispute
test his wisdom with hard questions after hearing of his fame
form a military alliance against Egypt
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 10:1-3 describes the Queen of Sheba coming to test Solomon with difficult questions after hearing reports of his wisdom, and finding it even greater than reported.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Solomon's Temple in Jerusalem was built primarily to
options: house the tombs of Israel's former kings
store the nation's gold and treasures
serve as Solomon's royal palace
serve as a permanent house of worship for the God of Israel
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 6 describes the construction of the Temple as a permanent dwelling place for God's presence and the centre of Israelite worship, replacing the portable tabernacle.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Rehoboam's refusal to lighten his father Solomon's heavy labour demands led directly to
options: the reunification of all twelve tribes
a lasting peace treaty with Egypt
the immediate destruction of Jerusalem
the northern tribes rebelling and forming a separate kingdom under Jeroboam
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 12 recounts how Rehoboam's harsh response to the people's plea for relief caused the ten northern tribes to revolt and follow Jeroboam, splitting the kingdom.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Jeroboam, first king of the northern kingdom of Israel, led the people into sin chiefly by
options: forming an alliance with the Assyrian empire
reinstating Saul's descendants to positions of power
rebuilding altars to the God of Israel in every town
setting up golden calves at Bethel and Dan for worship
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 12:28-30 describes Jeroboam setting up golden calves so his subjects would not return to Jerusalem to worship, leading Israel into idolatry.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: King Ahab's marriage to Jezebel led Israel deeper into idolatry mainly through the promotion of the worship of
options: Chemosh
Dagon
Baal
Molech
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 16:31-33 records that Ahab's marriage to the Phoenician princess Jezebel led to widespread promotion of Baal worship throughout Israel.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Elijah's contest with the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel was designed to demonstrate that
options: sacrifice alone could not please God
Israel needed a new king to restore true worship
the Lord, not Baal, was the true God who answered by fire
prophets should never challenge a reigning king
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 18:20-39 recounts Elijah's contest, in which fire fell from heaven upon his sacrifice, proving decisively that the Lord alone is God.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Elijah's dramatic encounter with God at Mount Horeb, after fleeing from Jezebel, revealed God's presence not in the wind, earthquake, or fire, but in
options: a loud trumpet blast
a burning bush
a still, small voice
a pillar of cloud
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 19:11-13 describes God revealing Himself to Elijah not through dramatic natural phenomena but through a gentle whisper or still small voice.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Naboth's vineyard, which King Ahab coveted, was seized through Jezebel's scheme involving
options: false witnesses who accused Naboth of blasphemy, leading to his execution
a rigged court case over unpaid taxes
a forged deed of sale
a bribe paid to Naboth's sons
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 21 describes Jezebel's plot using false witnesses to falsely accuse Naboth of cursing God and the king, resulting in his stoning and the seizure of his vineyard.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Elisha's request to Elijah before his master was taken up to heaven was for
options: a written record of all Elijah's prophecies
the position of chief priest in Israel
a double portion of Elijah's spirit
control over the northern kingdom's army
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 2:9 records Elisha's request for a double portion of Elijah's spirit as he prepared to continue Elijah's prophetic ministry.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The prophet Amos, though from Judah, directed most of his prophetic warnings to
options: the exiles already living in Babylon
the Assyrian empire, warning of coming judgement
the northern kingdom of Israel, condemning social injustice
the priests of Judah alone
questions.explanation: Amos, a shepherd from Tekoa in Judah, was sent to prophesy against the northern kingdom of Israel, strongly denouncing its social injustice and oppression of the poor.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Amos famously declared that God desired, above empty religious festivals and sacrifices, that
options: the northern and southern kingdoms reunite
the monarchy be abolished entirely
the Temple in Jerusalem be rebuilt immediately
justice roll on like a river and righteousness like a never-failing stream
questions.explanation: Amos 5:24 records this well-known call for genuine justice and righteousness to flow continually, rather than empty ritual observance.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Hosea's marriage to Gomer, an unfaithful wife, was used by God to illustrate
options: the need for stricter marriage laws in Israel
the political alliance between Israel and Judah
Israel's spiritual unfaithfulness and God's persistent, redeeming love
the coming exile of Judah to Babylon
questions.explanation: Hosea 1-3 uses the prophet's painful marriage as a living parable of Israel's unfaithfulness to God and God's unwavering, redeeming love in pursuing reconciliation.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Isaiah's vision of God's glory that inaugurated his prophetic ministry took place
options: in the Temple, in the year King Uzziah died
beside the river Chebar in Babylon
on Mount Carmel during a contest with false prophets
in a vision of a valley of dry bones
questions.explanation: Isaiah 6:1 records that Isaiah's vision of the Lord's glory, attended by seraphim, occurred in the Temple in the year King Uzziah died.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The northern kingdom of Israel fell to which foreign empire in 722 BC?
options: Egypt
Persia
Babylon
Assyria
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 17 records the fall of Samaria, the capital of the northern kingdom, to the Assyrian empire in 722 BC, resulting in the exile of many Israelites.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The southern kingdom of Judah was eventually conquered and its people taken into exile by
options: the Persians under Cyrus
the Assyrians under Sennacherib
the Babylonians under Nebuchadnezzar
the Egyptians under Pharaoh Necho
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 25 describes the fall of Jerusalem and the exile of Judah's people to Babylon under King Nebuchadnezzar in the early sixth century BC.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The Babylonian exile is generally interpreted by the prophets as God's judgement primarily upon Judah's
options: failure to build a strong enough army
refusal to pay tribute to foreign kings
neglect of agricultural land
persistent idolatry and disobedience to the covenant
questions.explanation: The prophetic writings consistently interpret the exile as covenant judgement for Judah's long history of idolatry and disobedience to God's law.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Daniel and his three friends were taken to Babylon as young exiles and chose to remain faithful to God chiefly by
options: refusing to learn the language of the Chaldeans
refusing to defile themselves with the king's food and wine
leading a rebellion against Babylonian rule
hiding from the king's officials entirely
questions.explanation: Daniel 1 records how Daniel and his friends resolved not to defile themselves with the royal food and wine, choosing a diet of vegetables and water instead.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Daniel's three friends, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, were thrown into a fiery furnace for
options: revealing the king's dream without permission
stealing from the royal treasury
refusing to serve in the king's court
refusing to bow down to King Nebuchadnezzar's golden image
questions.explanation: Daniel 3 recounts how the three men were cast into the fiery furnace for refusing to worship the golden image Nebuchadnezzar had set up, yet were miraculously preserved.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Daniel was thrown into the den of lions after
options: he was falsely accused of theft
he refused to interpret the king's dream
he continued praying to God despite a royal decree forbidding it
he criticised the king publicly at a banquet
questions.explanation: Daniel 6 describes how Daniel's enemies used a royal decree against prayer to trap him, but he continued praying openly to God and was thrown to the lions, from which God delivered him.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The Persian king who eventually issued a decree allowing the Jewish exiles to return home and rebuild the Temple was
options: Nebuchadnezzar
Xerxes
Cyrus
Darius
questions.explanation: Ezra 1:1-4 records the decree of Cyrus, king of Persia, permitting the Jewish exiles to return to Jerusalem and rebuild the Temple of the Lord.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Zerubbabel is chiefly remembered in the post-exilic narrative for leading
options: the military defence of Jerusalem against the Samaritans
the compilation of the book of Psalms
the reconstruction of the city walls of Jerusalem
the first group of exiles back to Jerusalem and the rebuilding of the Temple
questions.explanation: Ezra 1-6 describes Zerubbabel leading the returning exiles and overseeing the rebuilding of the Temple, later completed under the prophets Haggai and Zechariah's encouragement.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Ezra the scribe is particularly noted in the post-exilic period for his work in
options: leading a military campaign against Persia
teaching and re-establishing the Law of Moses among the returned exiles
rebuilding the walls of Jerusalem
constructing a second royal palace
questions.explanation: Ezra 7-10 presents Ezra as a scribe devoted to studying and teaching the Law of the Lord, leading spiritual reform among the returned community.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Nehemiah's primary achievement upon returning to Jerusalem was
options: rebuilding the city walls of Jerusalem despite strong opposition
establishing the office of high priest
translating the scriptures into Aramaic
constructing the second Temple from its foundation
questions.explanation: The Book of Nehemiah recounts his leadership in rebuilding Jerusalem's broken walls in fifty-two days, despite opposition from Sanballat and Tobiah.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Esther risked her life before the Persian king mainly to
options: negotiate a peace treaty with a foreign nation
request the rebuilding of the Jerusalem Temple
save the Jewish people from Haman's plot of extermination
secure her own position as queen permanently
questions.explanation: The Book of Esther recounts how Queen Esther courageously approached King Xerxes uninvited to expose Haman's plot and save the Jewish people from destruction.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: According to Luke's Gospel, the angel Gabriel announced the birth of Jesus to Mary in the town of
options: Nazareth
Bethlehem
Capernaum
Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Luke 1:26-31 records Gabriel's announcement to Mary in Nazareth, a town in Galilee, that she would conceive and give birth to Jesus.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Jesus was born in Bethlehem because Joseph and Mary had travelled there to
options: register in a census ordered by Caesar Augustus
seek healing at the Temple
visit relatives during a religious festival
escape persecution in Nazareth
questions.explanation: Luke 2:1-7 explains that Joseph and Mary journeyed to Bethlehem, the city of David, to register for a census decreed by Caesar Augustus, where Jesus was born.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: According to Matthew's Gospel, the wise men who visited the infant Jesus were guided by
options: the prophet Simeon in the Temple
a star they had seen in the east
an angel who appeared to them directly
a dream given to each of them beforehand
questions.explanation: Matthew 2:1-2, 9-10 describes the Magi following a star that led them from the east to the place where the young child was.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: King Herod's response to news of the birth of a 'king of the Jews' was to order
options: the immediate arrest of the wise men
a nationwide census of all newborns
a public celebration throughout Judea
the massacre of male infants in and around Bethlehem
questions.explanation: Matthew 2:16 records Herod's brutal order to kill all boys two years old and under in Bethlehem, after being deceived by the wise men.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: John the Baptist's ministry in the wilderness was chiefly characterised by his call for people to
options: pay tribute to the Roman governor
join him in armed resistance against Rome
repent and be baptised in preparation for the coming Messiah
rebuild the Jerusalem Temple
questions.explanation: The Gospels describe John the Baptist preaching a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins, preparing the way for the Messiah.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: At Jesus' baptism in the Jordan River, the voice from heaven declared Him to be
options: the returning Elijah
the promised prophet like Moses
God's beloved Son, in whom He was well pleased
the new high priest of Israel
questions.explanation: Matthew 3:16-17 records the heavenly voice affirming Jesus as God's beloved Son at His baptism, as the Spirit descended like a dove.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: During His forty days in the wilderness, Satan's first temptation urged Jesus to
options: worship Satan in exchange for all the kingdoms of the world
turn water into wine at a wedding
throw Himself from the pinnacle of the Temple
turn stones into bread to satisfy His hunger
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:3 records Satan's first temptation, challenging Jesus to prove His identity by turning stones into bread after His long fast.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Jesus performed His first recorded miracle, turning water into wine, at
options: a wedding in Cana of Galilee
the Sea of Galilee
the synagogue in Nazareth
the Temple courts in Jerusalem
questions.explanation: John 2:1-11 records Jesus' first miracle, turning water into wine at a wedding celebration in Cana of Galilee.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Jesus called His first disciples, Simon Peter and Andrew, while they were engaged in
options: fishing on the Sea of Galilee
tending sheep in the hills of Judea
collecting taxes at Capernaum
studying the Law in the synagogue
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:18-20 describes Jesus calling Simon Peter and his brother Andrew as they were casting their nets into the Sea of Galilee.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The miracle in which Jesus fed a large crowd using only five loaves and two fish is significant partly because it demonstrates
options: His fulfilment of the Passover sacrifice
His authority over unclean spirits
His teaching against wealth and possessions
His compassion and divine power to provide abundantly
questions.explanation: The feeding of the five thousand, recorded in all four Gospels, shows Jesus' compassion for the crowd and His miraculous power to provide for their needs abundantly.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Jesus raised Lazarus from the dead in the town of
options: Bethsaida
Bethany
Capernaum
Bethlehem
questions.explanation: John 11 recounts Jesus raising His friend Lazarus from the dead four days after his burial in the village of Bethany, near Jerusalem.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: At the Transfiguration, Jesus appeared in glory on the mountain alongside
options: Moses and Elijah
John the Baptist and Elijah
David and Solomon
Abraham and Isaac
questions.explanation: Matthew 17:1-3 describes Jesus being transfigured before Peter, James, and John, appearing with Moses and Elijah, representing the Law and the Prophets.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Jesus healed the man born blind in John's Gospel by
options: laying hands on the man's head in the Temple courts
simply speaking a word of command from a distance
making mud with saliva, applying it to the man's eyes, and sending him to wash in the Pool of Siloam
instructing the man's parents to pray fervently
questions.explanation: John 9:6-7 describes Jesus making mud from spittle, anointing the blind man's eyes, and instructing him to wash in the Pool of Siloam, after which he could see.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Jesus' encounter with the Samaritan woman at the well took place near the town of
options: Sychar
Cana
Emmaus
Jericho
questions.explanation: John 4:5-7 sets Jesus' conversation with the Samaritan woman at Jacob's well, near the Samaritan town of Sychar.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Zacchaeus, the wealthy tax collector, first encountered Jesus by
options: climbing a sycamore tree to see Him over the crowd
waiting at the Temple gate for Jesus to pass
sending a servant to invite Jesus to dinner
following Jesus secretly at night
questions.explanation: Luke 19:1-4 describes Zacchaeus, being short in stature, climbing a sycamore tree to catch a glimpse of Jesus passing through Jericho.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Jesus' entry into Jerusalem, celebrated as Palm Sunday, was marked by the crowd
options: presenting Him with royal garments and a crown
offering animal sacrifices along His path
spreading their cloaks and palm branches on the road while shouting 'Hosanna'
singing psalms exclusively reserved for the high priest
questions.explanation: Matthew 21:8-9 and John 12:12-13 describe the crowd welcoming Jesus into Jerusalem by laying down cloaks and palm branches while shouting 'Hosanna' in celebration.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Jesus' entry into Jerusalem riding on a donkey is understood as a fulfilment of the prophecy in
options: Isaiah, concerning a suffering servant
Zechariah, concerning a king coming humbly on a donkey
Micah, concerning the birthplace of the Messiah
Malachi, concerning a coming messenger
questions.explanation: Matthew 21:4-5 cites Zechariah 9:9, which foretold a king coming to Jerusalem, humble and mounted on a donkey.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Jesus' cleansing of the Temple involved Him driving out
options: the money changers and sellers of animals for sacrifice
the beggars who gathered near the entrance
the Pharisees who were teaching in the courts
the Roman soldiers stationed at the gates
questions.explanation: Matthew 21:12-13 records Jesus overturning the tables of money changers and driving out sellers, declaring that His Father's house should be a house of prayer.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: At the Last Supper, Jesus instituted what Christians now observe as
options: the sacrament of Holy Communion (the Eucharist)
the rite of baptism
the feast of Pentecost
the ceremony of foot washing alone
questions.explanation: Luke 22:19-20 records Jesus taking bread and wine, instructing His disciples to do this in remembrance of Him, establishing the Lord's Supper.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: During the Last Supper, Jesus predicted that Peter would
options: be the first disciple to be martyred
deny knowing Him three times before the rooster crowed
betray Him for thirty pieces of silver
flee to Galilee before the crucifixion
questions.explanation: Matthew 26:34 records Jesus foretelling that Peter would deny Him three times before the rooster crowed, a prophecy fulfilled during Jesus' trial.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Judas Iscariot agreed to betray Jesus to the chief priests in exchange for
options: safe passage out of Jerusalem
thirty pieces of silver
release from Roman taxation
a position of authority in the Sanhedrin
questions.explanation: Matthew 26:14-16 records that Judas agreed to betray Jesus for thirty pieces of silver, a sum paid by the chief priests.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: In the Garden of Gethsemane, Jesus prayed in deep anguish, asking God to
options: spare His disciples from any future persecution
send angels immediately to destroy His enemies
let the cup of suffering pass from Him, while submitting to God's will
reveal the identity of His betrayer publicly
questions.explanation: Matthew 26:39 records Jesus' anguished prayer asking that the cup pass from Him, yet ultimately submitting, 'not as I will, but as you will.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Judas identified Jesus to the arresting soldiers in Gethsemane by
options: handing the soldiers a written description
calling out His name loudly
pointing Him out from a distance
kissing Him
questions.explanation: Matthew 26:48-49 describes the prearranged signal in which Judas identified Jesus to the arresting party with a kiss.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: During Jesus' trial before the Sanhedrin, He was condemned chiefly on the charge of
options: blasphemy, for claiming to be the Son of God
violating the Sabbath through healing
inciting rebellion against Roman taxation
theft from the Temple treasury
questions.explanation: Matthew 26:63-66 records the high priest charging Jesus with blasphemy after He affirmed being the Son of God, leading the Sanhedrin to condemn Him as deserving death.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Pontius Pilate, the Roman governor, offered the crowd a choice to release Jesus or
options: one of the Sanhedrin's own members
Barabbas, a notorious prisoner
a Zealot leader awaiting trial
a Roman centurion accused of treason
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:15-21 describes Pilate's custom of releasing a prisoner at Passover, offering the crowd a choice between Jesus and the notorious prisoner Barabbas.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: In the Sermon on the Mount, the Beatitudes begin with the declaration that blessed are
options: the powerful, for they shall rule
the proud, for they shall be exalted
the wealthy, for they shall inherit the earth
the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven
questions.explanation: Matthew 5:3 opens the Beatitudes with the blessing on the poor in spirit, to whom the kingdom of heaven belongs.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus taught that His followers should be the 'salt of the earth' and
options: 'the light of the world'
'the builders of the temple'
'the keepers of the law'
'the shepherds of the flock'
questions.explanation: Matthew 5:13-14 pairs the metaphor of salt of the earth with Jesus' description of His followers as 'the light of the world.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Jesus taught His disciples a model prayer, commonly called the Lord's Prayer, which begins
options: 'O Lord, hear my cry and answer me'
'Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name'
'Blessed are you, Lord our God, King of the universe'
'Glory to God in the highest'
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:9-13 records the Lord's Prayer, beginning 'Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name,' as a model for how Jesus' disciples should pray.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: In the Parable of the Sower, the seed that fell among thorns and was choked represents those who
options: hear the word and produce a bountiful harvest
never hear the word being preached at all
hear the word, but the worries of life and deceitfulness of wealth choke it
hear the word and immediately reject it outright
questions.explanation: Matthew 13:22 explains that the seed among thorns represents those who hear the word, but worldly worries and the deceitfulness of wealth choke it, making it unfruitful.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: In the Parable of the Good Samaritan, the central lesson Jesus taught concerned
options: showing mercy and love to one's neighbour regardless of social or ethnic barriers
the duty of priests to perform Temple sacrifices faithfully
the importance of strict observance of the Sabbath
the need to pay taxes to Caesar
questions.explanation: Luke 10:25-37 uses the parable of the Good Samaritan to teach that true neighbourly love crosses ethnic and social boundaries, exemplified by the despised Samaritan's compassion.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: In the Parable of the Prodigal Son, the father's reaction upon his younger son's return demonstrates God's
options: indifference toward the son's earlier rebellion
strict justice in demanding repayment of the wasted inheritance
forgiving and gracious love toward the repentant sinner
reluctance to forgive without a period of punishment
questions.explanation: Luke 15:20-24 shows the father running to embrace his returning son, illustrating God's readiness to forgive and joyfully welcome back the repentant sinner.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: In the Parable of the Talents, the servant who was condemned was the one who
options: doubled his talent through wise investment
buried his talent out of fear instead of investing it
gave his talent away to the poor
invested his talent but lost it in a bad venture
questions.explanation: Matthew 25:24-30 describes the servant who, out of fear, buried his one talent rather than putting it to use, and was condemned as wicked and lazy.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Jesus' Parable of the Lost Sheep teaches primarily about
options: the need for unity among the twelve apostles
the importance of counting one's possessions carefully
the duty of shepherds to protect their flocks from wolves
God's joy over the recovery of even a single repentant sinner
questions.explanation: Luke 15:4-7 describes the shepherd's joy at finding one lost sheep, illustrating heaven's rejoicing over a single sinner who repents.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: When asked which was the greatest commandment, Jesus replied that it was to
options: love the Lord your God with all your heart, soul, and mind
keep the entire Sabbath without exception
honour your father and mother above all
give generously to the Temple treasury
questions.explanation: Matthew 22:37-38 records Jesus identifying love for God with all one's heart, soul, and mind as the greatest and first commandment.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The Day of Pentecost, marking the beginning of the Church's public ministry, was characterised primarily by
options: the conversion of Saul on the road to Damascus
the appointment of the first seven deacons
the stoning of Stephen before the Sanhedrin
the Holy Spirit descending upon the disciples, enabling them to speak in other tongues
questions.explanation: Acts 2:1-4 describes the dramatic outpouring of the Holy Spirit on the disciples at Pentecost, enabling them to speak in various languages to the gathered crowd.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Peter's sermon on the Day of Pentecost resulted in
options: the conversion of the Roman governor
the immediate arrest of all the apostles
about three thousand people being baptised and added to the believers
a riot that scattered the early believers
questions.explanation: Acts 2:41 records that about three thousand people responded to Peter's Pentecost sermon, were baptised, and joined the growing community of believers.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The early believers in Jerusalem, as described in Acts, were noted for their practice of
options: sharing their possessions and meeting one another's needs in fellowship
avoiding all contact with non-believers
meeting only in secret to escape detection
rejecting the Jewish scriptures entirely
questions.explanation: Acts 2:44-45 describes the early Christian community holding possessions in common and distributing to anyone in need, reflecting deep fellowship.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Ananias and Sapphira met with sudden death in the early church after
options: openly denying that Jesus had risen from the dead
refusing to be baptised with the other believers
lying to the Holy Spirit about the proceeds from the sale of their property
leading a rebellion against the apostles' authority
questions.explanation: Acts 5:1-10 recounts how Ananias and Sapphira fell dead after deceitfully withholding part of the proceeds from a land sale while claiming to give it all, thereby lying to the Holy Spirit.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The seven men chosen in Acts 6, including Stephen, were appointed primarily to
options: serve as judges over civil disputes among believers
replace the twelve apostles as the church's leaders
lead the church's mission to the Gentiles exclusively
oversee the daily distribution of food to widows in the church
questions.explanation: Acts 6:1-6 describes the appointment of seven men, including Stephen, to manage the daily distribution of food, resolving a dispute over the neglect of Greek-speaking widows.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Stephen, the first Christian martyr, was stoned to death after he was accused of
options: stealing from the Temple treasury
practising sorcery among the people
speaking against the Temple and the Law of Moses
leading an armed uprising against Rome
questions.explanation: Acts 6:11-14 records the false accusations brought against Stephen concerning blasphemy against the Temple and the Law, which led to his trial and stoning.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Saul of Tarsus, before his conversion, was known chiefly for his
options: zealous persecution of the early Christian church
role as a tax collector for Rome
position as a Roman centurion in Judea
generous support of the apostles' ministry
questions.explanation: Acts 8:3 and 9:1-2 describe Saul's fierce persecution of believers before his dramatic conversion on the road to Damascus.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Saul's conversion took place on the road to
options: Antioch
Jericho
Damascus
Emmaus
questions.explanation: Acts 9:1-9 recounts Saul's encounter with the risen Christ in a blinding light on the road to Damascus, which led to his conversion and later ministry as Paul.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Peter's vision of a sheet containing various animals, given while he was in Joppa, led him to understand that
options: certain dietary laws needed to be enforced more strictly
animal sacrifice should be reinstated in Christian worship
he should relocate the church's headquarters to Joppa
the gospel was also for the Gentiles, and no person should be called unclean
questions.explanation: Acts 10 describes Peter's vision preparing him to visit the Gentile centurion Cornelius, teaching him that God shows no partiality and that the gospel extends to all peoples.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: Cornelius, whose household became among the first Gentile converts, was described as
options: a Samaritan merchant living in Joppa
a Jewish high priest in Caesarea
a devout and God-fearing Roman centurion
a member of the Sanhedrin in Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Acts 10:1-2 introduces Cornelius as a devout, God-fearing centurion of the Italian Regiment stationed in Caesarea, whose household received the Holy Spirit.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: According to Paul's letter to the Galatians, the 'fruit of the Spirit' begins with
options: power, might, and dominion
wisdom, knowledge, and understanding
faith, hope, and charity
love, joy, and peace
questions.explanation: Galatians 5:22-23 lists the fruit of the Spirit beginning with love, joy, and peace, followed by patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, and self-control.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: In 1 Corinthians 13, often called the 'love chapter', Paul teaches that without love, even great gifts such as prophecy and knowledge are
options: reserved only for apostles
signs of spiritual maturity
sufficient for salvation
worthless
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 13:1-3 declares that without love, even impressive spiritual gifts and sacrificial acts amount to nothing.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: According to 1 Corinthians 13, love is described as being patient and kind, and it
options: does not envy, does not boast, and is not proud
seeks its own advantage above others
keeps a careful record of wrongs suffered
delights in the failures of others
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 13:4 describes love as patient and kind, free from envy, boasting, and pride.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: The Christian virtue of humility is most vividly modelled in the New Testament by Jesus' act of
options: calming the storm on the Sea of Galilee
multiplying the loaves and fishes
washing His disciples' feet at the Last Supper
cleansing the Temple courts
questions.explanation: John 13:3-15 describes Jesus humbling Himself to wash His disciples' feet, setting an example of humble service for them to follow.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.text: James' epistle teaches that genuine Christian faith must be accompanied by
options: strict avoidance of all Gentiles
good works, since faith without works is dead
wealth given generously to the Temple
elaborate ritual and ceremony
questions.explanation: James 2:14-17 argues that faith without accompanying good deeds is dead, emphasising that authentic faith produces practical action.
